data.reasoning: The only valid voting model (deepseek) reviewed all files, including the desktop entry, and found no malicious indicators. The PKGBUILD uses pinned sources with checksums and standard Rust build steps. The inconclusive result from qwen was due to a transient API error (HTTP 400) on noita_proxy.desktop, which carries no verdict signal. The advisory report from openrouter corroborates the safety.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error in the qwen model, which failed to review noita_proxy.desktop due to an HTTP 400 API error, resulting in an inconclusive overall verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed the same file and found it safe.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review noita_proxy.desktop due to an LLM API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError).
learnings: Transient API errors on individual files should not necessarily block the entire audit verdict if the file is successfully reviewed by another model or if the error can be retried.
The audit tool should gracefully handle partial API failures and either retry the specific file or rely on consensus from other models that successfully processed the file.
